fact: The DGSF says PNF II aims at digitising and centralising land documents and data nationwide, in a land information system that will be operational soon.
Newsmada reports ProPFR digitised land data in the Analamanga region and piloted an interconnected land information system linking topographic circumscriptions and land offices.

PRODUIR reports that after dematerialising legal-status certificates and topographic plans for Antananarivo, an automatic information kiosk entered public service on 7 July 2025 at the Tana-ville land office, issuing registration and legal-status certificates and individual plans.
Newsmada reports Madagascar's land system still rests on century-old, often incomplete or deteriorated archives, and that South Korea intends to support digitising land data.

Madagascar's decentralisation and land-planning ministry said in April 2025 that its land information system (SIF) will be deployed progressively in five pilot regions under National Land Programme II.

FAO says Madagascar's World Bank-backed CASEF project has certified 1.1 million parcels with QR-coded certificates linked to a digital version that will be stored in a national register once the system is fully implemented, with computers supplied to over 400 municipal land offices.
